goal: Help one household budget owner capture expenses and refunds, review signed daily activity, understand reconciled monthly category totals, and safely correct or undo mistakes on a phone.

requirements.description: Expense and refund variants both have explicit create and prefilled correction states; forms use a positive entered magnitude and explain Ledgerly's signed aggregation rule.
Today exposes one frequent Add expense action; the valid expense form is recognizable, has one Close dismissal and one active Save expense completion action.

The invalid transaction form retains entered content, explains both errors inline, disables completion, and offers only the top Close dismissal; rows visibly disclose editable expense and refund correction paths.
Edit overflow reveals a text-led neutral-surface delete action, strong destructive fill appears only on the named final confirmation, and the result recalculates totals with immediate Undo.

The transaction collection covers empty, one item with missing optional note, typical, a 25-item dense state with a visible total and scroll cue, and long content including a clearly labeled refund without shifting the shell.

The month view shows six category net totals and exact budget arithmetic; Groceries identifies eight expenses plus one refund, shows their signed net total, and provides an honest scroll cue to all nine contributors.
Every displayed daily total, count, category net total, remainder, percentage, refund adjustment, and post-delete balance follows the documented USD sign and budget contracts.
Dense, long-content, nested, validation, and destructive states remain readable across every delivery device, use honest reachability cues, and avoid repeated secondary-action noise.

Every collection state keeps the same Ledgerly/month header, Today–Month order, selected treatment, data-first start, and recurring budget metrics; forms and sheets use one compact task shell and one contextual dismissal.
Refund controls, labels, glyphs, and negative values consistently use the credit-green semantic treatment; coral is reserved for validation and destructive risk.
